title: RFMVDA: An Enhanced Deep Learning Approach for Customer Behavior Classification in E-Commerce Environments
authors: Kim, K.; Jo, M.; Ra, I.; Park, S.
tldr: Extends the RFM model with Visits, Durations, and Actions to classify both purchasing and non-purchasing e-commerce customers, achieving 92.98% segmentation prediction accuracy with a DNN.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional RFM models fail to capture continuous and diverse customer behaviors in e-commerce, as they focus only on purchasing customers and ignore non-purchasing visitors. This limits the ability to understand and target the full customer journey in online environments.
approach: Proposes RFMVDA model adding Visits, Durations, Actions to RFM for purchasing customers.
Proposes VDAR model using Visits, Durations, Actions, Referral Keyword for non-purchasing customers.
Models customer data into three components: information, session, and behavior units.
Implements a DNN with two hidden layers of 128 neurons each, using ReLU and sigmoid activations.
Uses categorical cross-entropy loss and Adam optimizer for multi-class classification.
Trains on a 3-month dataset from a South Korean e-commerce site with 9,416 customers.
Performs hyperparameter tuning via grid search and repeated stratified K-fold cross-validation.
Evaluates model with RMSE, Macro F1 Score, and Micro F1 Score metrics.
Analyzes feature importance using SHAP values.
Compares segmentation results against the LRFM model.
findings: num: The RFMVDA model achieved a segmentation prediction accuracy of 92.98%.
num: Training accuracy reached 99.54% with the optimal DNN configuration.
num: Repeated stratified K-fold cross-validation yielded an average accuracy of 96.9%.
num: The best hyperparameter configuration included ReLU activation, batch size 32, dropout rate 0.2, 200 epochs, and Adam optimizer.
num: RMSE for the 80%-20% split was 1.1778, indicating low prediction error.
num: Macro F1 Score was 0.7923 and Micro F1 Score was 0.9390 for the 80%-20% split.
Session duration, first action time, and desktop visits were the most influential features for segmentation.
The VDAR model segmented 4,742 non-purchasing customers into 9 distinct behavior-based groups.
RFMVDA reclassified 16 of 140 LRFM-defined 'Lost Customers' as 'Potential Loyal Customers'.
The RFMVDA model produced 14 distinct customer segments, compared to 4 from the LRFM model.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a new behavioral segmentation model (RFMVDA) that addresses the limitations of traditional RFM-based approaches in e-commerce settings. It demonstrates that incorporating non-transactional behavioral dimensions significantly improves the granularity of customer classification. The work also provides a methodology for segmenting non-purchasing customers using the VDAR model, a gap not previously addressed in the literature. Empirically, it validates the approach using real-world e-commerce data and a Deep Neural Network, showing strong predictive performance.
directly_justifies: Traditional RFM models fail to capture non-purchasing customer behavior in e-commerce.
The RFMVDA model achieves 92.98% segmentation prediction accuracy.
The VDAR model segments non-purchasing customers into distinct behavioral groups.
DNNs are well-suited for modeling complex customer behavior patterns in large e-commerce datasets.
limits: The analysis is based on a single e-commerce website over a 3-month period, which may not generalize to other contexts or capture seasonal trends.
The paper does not perform direct comparisons with other machine learning algorithms like Random Forests or Gradient Boosting.
No quantitative link is established between segmentation outcomes and financial metrics such as customer lifetime value.
The study does not address how the model would perform with sparse data typical of new users.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: A systematic scan across all topic domains was performed. The paper's core contribution falls under domains 3 (Expense Categorization Frameworks), 4 (Limitations and Gaps in Existing Systems), 5 (Financial Behavioral Profiles and Classification), and 12 (Evaluation Frameworks). Topic 3.A was selected as medium relevance due to the proposal of the RFMVDA segmentation framework. Topics 4.B and 5.C were rated high as the paper directly criticizes existing models and proposes a new classification approach. Topic 12.B was rated high for its thorough algorithmic evaluation. Domains such as 7 (Budgeting) and 8 (Anomaly Detection) were considered but rejected as the paper does not address budget recommendation or anomaly detection directly, though some contextual relevance exists. Topics related to Filipino professionals, cultural practices, and mobile-first design (1.A-2.D, 9.A-9.C) were rejected as the paper focuses on a general South Korean e-commerce context. Privacy (10.A-10.C) and Engagement (11.A-11.B) are not addressed. Synthetic data, deployment, and savings/debt management (13.A-14.C) are also not covered.
